title: Inner Product Decomposition — The Key Identity
content:
The central algebraic identity: for unit vector $n$ and arbitrary $u, v$,
$$\langle u, v \rangle = \langle u, n \rangle \langle v, n \rangle + \langle u^\perp, v^\perp \rangle$$
where $u^\perp = u - \langle u, n \rangle n$ is the perpendicular projection. The proof expands $\langle u - \langle u,n \rangle n,\, v - \langle v,n \rangle n \rangle$ using bilinearity and $\langle n, n \rangle = 1$. This single identity drives the entire spherical law of cosines.
mathContext: $\langle u, v \rangle = \langle u, n \rangle \langle v, n \rangle + \langle u - \langle u,n \rangle n,\; v - \langle v,n \rangle n \rangle$

title: Arc Length on the Unit Sphere
content: Arc length between unit vectors $u, v \in S^2$ is defined as $d(u,v) = \arccos(\langle u, v \rangle)$. Since $|\langle u,v \rangle| \leq 1$ by Cauchy-Schwarz and $\|u\| = \|v\| = 1$, the arccos is well-defined. Properties proved: non-negativity, $d \leq \pi$, $\cos(d(u,v)) = \langle u,v \rangle$ (the key recovery formula), $d(u,u) = 0$, and symmetry $d(u,v) = d(v,u)$.

title: Perpendicular Projection Norm Equals Sine of Arc Length
content: For unit vectors $u, n$: $\|\text{proj}^\perp(u,n)\| = \sin(\text{arcLength}(u,n))$. Proved via the Pythagorean identity: $\|u\|^2 = \langle u,n \rangle^2 + \|u^\perp\|^2$ gives $1 = \cos^2\theta + \|u^\perp\|^2$, so $\|u^\perp\|^2 = \sin^2\theta$. Non-negativity of both sides (using $\sin \geq 0$ on $[0,\pi]$) gives $\|u^\perp\| = \sin\theta$.

title: Spherical Law of Cosines — Algebraic Form
content: For unit vectors $A, B, C \in S^2$: $\langle A, B \rangle = \langle A, C \rangle \langle B, C \rangle + \langle A^\perp_C, B^\perp_C \rangle$. This is the direct application of inner_decomposition with $n = C$. The algebraic form is the 'engine room' — all trigonometric statements follow from translating inner products to cosines and projection norms to sines.
mathContext: $\langle A, B \rangle = \langle A, C \rangle \langle B, C \rangle + \langle \text{proj}^\perp_C A,\, \text{proj}^\perp_C B \rangle$

title: Spherical Law of Cosines — Trigonometric Form
content: The main theorem: $\cos(c) = \cos(b) \cdot \cos(a) + \langle A^\perp_C, B^\perp_C \rangle$, where $a, b, c$ are arc-length sides of the spherical triangle. When the projections are non-zero (non-degenerate triangle), the inner product of projections equals $\sin(b) \cdot \sin(a) \cdot \cos(C)$, recovering the classical formula $\cos(c) = \cos(a)\cos(b) + \sin(a)\sin(b)\cos(C)$.
mathContext: $\cos c = \cos a \cdot \cos b + \sin a \cdot \sin b \cdot \cos C$

title: Spherical Triangle Structure
content: A spherical triangle is defined by three unit vectors $A, B, C \in S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$. The sides are arc lengths between vertex pairs: $a = d(B,C)$ (opposite $A$), $b = d(A,C)$ (opposite $B$), $c = d(A,B)$ (opposite $C$). Each side is in $[0, \pi]$. The dihedral angle at vertex $C$ is the angle between the tangent vectors to the great circle arcs $CA$ and $CB$.
mathContext: $a = \arccos(\langle B, C \rangle),\quad b = \arccos(\langle A, C \rangle),\quad c = \arccos(\langle A, B \rangle)$

title: Small-Angle Limit Recovers Planar Law of Cosines
content: In the limit of small sides ($a, b, c \to 0$), Taylor expansion gives $\cos x \approx 1 - x^2/2$ and $\sin x \approx x$, so $\cos(c) \approx 1 - c^2/2$ and $\cos(a)\cos(b) + \sin(a)\sin(b)\cos(C) \approx 1 - a^2/2 - b^2/2 + ab\cos(C)$. Equating: $c^2 \approx a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos(C)$, the planar law of cosines. This is the geometric manifestation of curvature $\kappa \to 0$.
mathContext: $\cos c \approx 1 - \frac{c^2}{2},\quad \sin x \approx x \implies c^2 \approx a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C$
